Every question in quiz.json tests a point about the target of the change: runScenario refuses a secret or model key shorter than 8 characters as a scenario problem, because the scrub rewrites every occurrence of a raw secret, JSON keys included, and a 1-character key broke the result directory after model calls were spent.

Every question sits at mechanism or design or trivial altitude: the inputs, state, invariants, and failure modes of the one mechanism the change targets, above function names and signatures; the problem the change solves, the shape chosen, the alternatives, and what it makes easy or hard next, above function names and flags; the intent and impact of the change, if anything
No question asks about these incidental parts of the change: the design doc wording; the test expectations
Every wrong option of a single or multi question is a plausible misreading of the change, not filler
Each question's key_points state what a correct answer must cover, at the same altitude as the question

The questions go outside in: the first ones cover what the change is for and its main boundary, narrower mechanisms and details come later, and no question is more central to the change than one asked before it, except the last
When quiz.json has two or more questions, the last one applies several points of the change to one new case the change does not spell out
